messages:
anika: Canary rollout for model v2.3.1 is blocked - 99p latency jumped from ~90ms to ~230ms on several routes. Need triage ASAP.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: canary-2026-03-03-11:05 (model v2.3.1) - monitoring enabled

sre-bot: Alert: latency_99p > threshold on canary cluster (svc-inference-1). Spike observed at ~11:07 UTC

mike: ack. which routes showing the spike? all chat or specific paths?

anika: Mostly chat-stream and text-gen routes. Logs show a small % of requests with much longer tokenized sequences; KV cache miss rate up ~40% for those.

jessica: Quick profiler dump from a canary node (11:08):
```
# breakdown (tail sample)
tokenize    : 12ms
kernel_sel  : 18ms -> fallback to ref kernel
kv_lookup   : 20ms (miss-heavy)
decode      : 150ms
total_99p   : 230ms
```

calvin: kernel_sel fallback? We didn't ship kernel changes in this deploy.

jessica: Right. But model-onboard changes modified the model config: `quant_backend` default was set to `auto` in the onboarding script, which allows runtime to pick a quant/kernel path that can trigger slower reference kernels on some HW.

mike: And the tokenizer?

anika: New checkpoint includes a tokenizer mapping update: adds explicit padding token and tweaks BPE for some rare sequences. Median token length +2, tail +30 for ~1.8% of requests. That increases KV cache churn.

calvin: Longer sequences + increased KV misses can easily magnify decode latency. Combine with a slower kernel and tail latency spikes.

jessica: I bisected: reverting PRs that set `quant_backend=auto` and the tokenizer mapping removes the spike. Isolating each: tokenizer change increases seq len and cache misses; quant_backend=auto causes kernel_selector to pick `ref_attn` on A100 in our compiled profiles.

mike: paste kernel selection logs?

jessica: log snippet:
```
[11:06:42] kernel_selector: requested='fused_attn_fast', available=['fused_attn_fast','ref_attn'], selected='ref_attn'
[11:06:42] kernel_selector: reason='bitwidth/profile_mismatch'
```

anika: So it's a config drift + tokenizer delta. Together they cause the 99p regression.

calvin: What did CI run for this onboarding PR? Did it include A100-like perf checks and tokenizer distribution diffs?

mike: CI runs unit tests and a basic perf smoke (tokens/sec, median latency). 99p and tokenizer distribution diffs are not gated per-PR; those perf tests run periodically but not on every onboarding merge. Looks like this PR didn't hit the full perf matrix.

jessica: I ran a local bisect across the onboarding commits: commit 7f3a2b4 changed quant_backend default; commit 9b2c1d updated tokenizer mapping. Either one alone reduces the regression; both together reproduce full spike.

anika: Action: revert the onboarding merge to unblock the rollout. Also add perf checks to onboarding pipeline. We might also do a quick hotpatch while the revert goes through.

calvin: I'll open the revert PR and add CI changes. @mike can you add a regression test that asserts 99p within 1.2x baseline for a canonical prompt set and a tokenizer-distribution check (<=1% diff) for onboarding?

mike: Yes. I'll add: (1) perf-lit test running 5k sample prompts asserting 99p < 1.2x baseline, (2) tokenizer invariant test comparing token length distribution on canonical prompts, (3) kernel-selection smoke test that flags `quant_backend=auto` selecting ref kernels on A100 SKU emulation.

jessica: Short-term mitigation I can push: normalize tokenizer output used for KV cache keys (strip trailing pad/eos so keys match previous runs) and force `quant_backend=native` on A100 until we validate kernels. I can prepare a canary hotpatch.

ops: Hotpatch OK, but prefer revert if it's faster to minimize churn.

deploy-bot: Hotpatch job queued: patch/tokenizer-kv-normalize -> canary-2026-03-03-11:40

sre-bot: Post-patch metrics: kv_miss_rate for affected routes dropped from +40% -> +6%, 99p reduced from 230ms -> 120ms. Partial improvement but not full baseline.

mike: Revert PR opened: revert PR #4278. It reverts the quant_backend default and tokenizer mapping. Unit tests pass; perf suite queued.

calvin: Also adding checklist items to model-onboard: run full perf suite (A100 profile) and tokenizer-diff check before merging; surface any default runtime flag changes in onboarding reviews.

anika: Revert merged at 11:55 UTC and rolled to canary.

deploy-bot: Revert deploy started: canary-2026-03-03-11:56 - rolling

sre-bot: Canary after revert: 99p stabilized at ~95ms, kv_miss back to baseline. kernel_selector shows 'fused_attn_fast' selected on A100.

jessica: Root cause summary: onboarding PR introduced (1) tokenizer mapping change increasing tokenized lengths for a tail of inputs, raising KV cache misses, and (2) a config default `quant_backend=auto` that triggered a conservative (slower) kernel on some hardware. Combined caused 99p regression.

mike: Long-term work: add onboarding perf gate, kernel-selection validation in CI, tokenizer distribution invariants, KV key normalization tests, and better perf signal coverage for 99p latency. I'll file tickets.

calvin: Created tickets: RUNTIME-3894 (onboard perf gate), RUNTIME-3895 (tokenizer-diff-check), RUNTIME-3896 (kernel-selection-smoke), RUNTIME-3897 (kv-key-normalization-test).

anika: Thanks all. Canary healthy at 12:05 UTC. Closing loop once tickets land on runtime backlog.
